explanation: A segmentation or bus error indicates a memory access fault reported by the operating system. The signal identifies the kind of failure but cannot identify a source line or prove a particular pointer mistake. Check the inputs and operations that read or write memory.
exampleExplanation: An array with three elements has indices 0, 1, and 2. The loop ends before attempting to access index 3.
misconceptions: The last message printed can precede the faulty instruction by several steps.
A program can read invalid memory without crashing. A run that exits normally is not proof of memory safety.

reference.title: Local C reference on bounds and object lifetime
reference.text: Access requires a live object and a valid index or pointer. Start with array bounds, pointer initialization, ownership of allocated memory, and addresses taken from variables that have gone out of lifetime. A signal alone cannot distinguish these from other access or alignment faults.
